subject: Competitive bake-off recap: ZenWell vendor comparison & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenwell.com>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@zenwell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: ZenWell vendor comparison & next steps

Thanks for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the bake-off.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- 95th pct latency spikes on peak traffic causing degraded search experience
- Cost variability across big model runs (hard to predict monthly spend)
- Integration complexity with your existing auth/OIDC and S3 data flow
- Need for stronger data residency controls for PHI-proxied records

Goals we heard:
- Reduce 95th pct inference latency by ~50–60% for the main search flow
- Keep incremental inference cost under $X per 1M tokens (we'll refine target once we have usage profile)
- Validate an integration path that supports your SSO + S3-based dataset without moving sensitive data off-cluster

Competitive context you mentioned:
- You're running parallel evaluations with OmniServe and Vertex AI; primary criteria are latency, cost, and ease of integration (SSO + data residency).

Proposed bake-off plan (attached: bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx):
1) Two-week evaluation window; Redwood will provide a hosted eval endpoint + instructions for an on-prem connector if needed.
2) Run three scenarios: small prompt/low-latency, medium prompt/production mix, large prompt/batch scoring.
3) We will collect token-level latency, p95/p99, and cost-per-1k-token estimates; Marissa (cc'd) will lead collection and reporting.
4) Security checklist: we confirm your requirement for KMS-backed keys and audit logs — we can provide KMS integration details during kickoff.

Open questions / ask from your side:
- Can you share a redacted sample of the input distribution (sizes and typical prompt shapes)?
- Do you require an on-prem connector from day 1, or is a hosted endpoint acceptable for initial perf runs?
- Who should we add to the test access (S3 path / service account)?

Next steps:
- Alex / Priya: confirm dataset access method and the primary contact for test credentials by EOD Thu (20 Aug).
- Redwood: share test endpoints, pricing proposal, and kickoff calendar invite (proposed Mon 24 Aug).

Appreciate the partnership — we'll make the bake-off easy to run and measurable.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

---

Thanks Jordan — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide a redacted sample dataset (no PHI) in an S3 bucket; however the final scoring run needs to happen in our VPC environment or through an approved on-prem connector due to compliance. Initial latency tests against a hosted endpoint are fine for a baseline.
- Primary contact for credentials: me (Alex) and Priya. We'll create an IAM role with limited read access to the test prefix and share an access method (role ARN or pre-signed URL).
- Cost target: we'll send a number, but for planning assume we need to be < $200 per 1M tokens for this workload.

We'll aim to have the dataset share + access method by Thu EOD. Can you also confirm whether Redwood can provide per-request tracing (trace-id) so we can correlate logs on our side?

On scheduling — Mon 24 Aug works for a 30–45 min kickoff (we're in US Pacific).

Appreciate it,
Alex

Thanks — I'll lead the bake-off setup from the Redwood side. Quick summary of what we'll deliver and remaining asks:

- Test harness (runbook + scripts) to exercise the three scenarios Jordan outlined
- Results template (attached: results-template.xlsx) with p50/p95/p99, average token cost, and raw request traces

- Mon 24 Aug: kickoff (30–45m) + sync on acceptance criteria
